title: Convert a public PIM Manager environment to private with one command
purpose: Converts a public (external) PIM Manager environment to private (internal-only) in one command. It runs the conversion guide's steps in order by calling the existing setup scripts (safety copy, private registry, remove and redeploy or rebuild, verify from inside the network, optional custom name, optional private SQL), checks each step before the next, records progress per tenant and resource group so -Resume continues after a stop or a failure, and stops with exit code 10 where your network team must act. Data is kept. It only prints the plan unless -Apply is given.
whenToRun: Once, to move a public PIM Manager environment to private, in a maintenance window of about 1-2 hours (the PIM Manager and the engine are unavailable from the removal until the redeploy completes; active privileged access stays active). Read network-options.md first. Run it from the PIM Manager release package folder (Pro / trial: the signed package Install-Invardia downloaded for your installation; Community: the public repository at the release tag), on the machine that ran the original install when possible (its deploy profile holds the install's parameters). It stops at two points: when -SkipPeering is given (the hub owner creates the hub side of the peering) and before any public endpoint is closed (verify from inside the network); resume with -Resume -Apply and -HubSideDone or -ConfirmedFromInside.

runAs.name: Owner, or Contributor + User Access Administrator
runAs.why: The steps it runs remove and recreate the Container Apps environment, the PIM Manager and the jobs, upgrade the registry and add private endpoints, and grant the new managed identities their Azure roles (AcrPull, Reader, Contributor for the updater).

runAs.name: Network Contributor
runAs.why: Only when this run creates the peering and links the private DNS zone to the hub. With -SkipPeering the hub owner does it with the script New-PimHubPrepareScript.ps1 writes, and this run needs no right on the hub.

runAs.name: Privileged Role Administrator
runAs.why: The redeploy grants the new identities their Microsoft Graph application permissions and adds them to the role-assignable SQL admin group.

runAs.name: Application Administrator
runAs.why: Sign-in (Easy Auth) is attached to the new private address: the existing sign-in app registration is reused and its reply address moved.

runAs.name: One REST session for -TenantId: the Invardia Support app session for that tenant, or your own browser sign-in
runAs.why: Every step runs in this process and reuses the one session; a session of another tenant is refused. No Azure CLI, no PowerShell modules.

changes.object: the conversion state %LOCALAPPDATA%\pim\convert\<tenant>-<resource group>.json (parameters without secrets, the completed steps, the restore point) and the safety-copy capture folder of the same name
changes.why: So -Resume continues after a stop or a failure, and so the live app definitions are kept before anything is removed.
changes.undo: Delete the file and the folder after the conversion is complete.

changes.object: the container registry: Premium, a private endpoint, the privatelink.azurecr.io zone and a build pool (New-PimHostingPrerequisites.ps1)
changes.why: A private environment pulls images and builds updates over the private endpoint.
changes.undo: The registry stays Premium (never downgraded); delete the private endpoint and the build pool in the portal if you go back to public.

changes.object: the Container Apps jobs, the PIM Manager app and the Container Apps environment, and the role assignments of their system identities (Remove-PimContainerStack.ps1; route Redeploy)
changes.why: The internal/external setting of a Container Apps environment cannot be changed.
changes.undo: The next step recreates them; to go back to public, run Invoke-PimDeployAll.ps1 with the original deploy profile and -Apply.

changes.object: the internal-only Container Apps environment, the PIM Manager, the engine, bootstrap and updater jobs, the peering to the hub and the private DNS zone for the new address (Invoke-PimDeployAll.ps1 -Exposure internal, or Rebuild-PimEnvInternal.ps1 on route Rebuild)
changes.scope: the resource group given (the peering: the PIM VNet and, with the right, the hub VNet)
changes.why: The private environment, on the same subnet, SQL database and registry.
changes.undo: Rebuild-PimEnvExternal.ps1 -Apply converts back to public (the address changes again).

changes.object: the new managed identities' Microsoft Graph application permissions, Azure roles and database users
changes.permission: the engine and PIM Manager permission sets of Invoke-PimDeployAll.ps1 (see its documentation page)
changes.scope: the tenant / the PIM resource group / the PIM database
changes.why: Recreated apps get new managed identities; the grants of the old ones no longer match.
changes.undo: Removed with the identities when the stack is removed again.

changes.object: optional: a custom host name with your certificate and its DNS record (Set-PimManagerCustomHost.ps1, with -HostName)
changes.scope: the PIM Manager app and an existing private DNS zone
changes.why: One stable address that survives future rebuilds.
changes.undo: Remove the custom domain from the app and the record from the zone.

changes.object: optional: the SQL private endpoint and the privatelink.database.windows.net zone (New-PimHostingPrerequisites.ps1 -SqlPrivateEndpoint, with -SqlPrivate), then one deploy that saves the private values in the deploy profile
changes.scope: the SQL server and the PIM VNet
changes.why: Step 7 of the guide, done last, after the private PIM Manager is verified from inside.
changes.undo: Delete the SQL private endpoint; the server's public access is not changed by this script.

parameters.name: TenantId
parameters.help: The PIM tenant. The REST session is pinned to it; a session or subscription of another tenant is refused.

parameters.name: SubscriptionId
parameters.help: The PIM subscription.

parameters.name: ResourceGroup
parameters.help: The PIM resource group (the conversion state is kept per tenant and resource group).

parameters.name: Route
parameters.help: Redeploy (guide Route B, default: remove the Container Apps stack and deploy it again internal-only from the install's parameters; grants everything the new identities need in one session) or Rebuild (guide Route A: capture, recreate and restore the live apps; keeps hand-made app changes, Windows only, the database users need a certificate identity afterwards).

parameters.name: DeployProfilePath
parameters.help: The original install's saved parameters (written by Invoke-PimDeployAll.ps1 -Apply), or the file Invardia's wizard regenerated from your install answers. Values given on the command line win.

parameters.name: Tag
parameters.help: A short label: the hosting prerequisites token and the capture file names.

parameters.name: Location
parameters.help: The Azure region of the environment.

parameters.name: VnetName
parameters.help: The existing PIM VNet.

parameters.name: VnetResourceGroup
parameters.help: The VNet's resource group. This command supports the VNet in the PIM resource group only (otherwise follow the guide's manual steps).

parameters.name: SubnetName
parameters.help: The existing Container Apps subnet.

parameters.name: VnetAddressPrefix
parameters.help: The existing VNet range (the prerequisites script never invents an address plan).

parameters.name: SubnetAddressPrefix
parameters.help: The existing Container Apps subnet range.

parameters.name: AcrName
parameters.help: The existing container registry.

parameters.name: LogAnalyticsName
parameters.help: The existing Log Analytics workspace.

parameters.name: SqlServerFqdn
parameters.help: The existing SQL server, e.g. <server>.database.windows.net.

parameters.name: SqlDatabase
parameters.help: The PIM database.

parameters.name: EnvName
parameters.help: The Container Apps environment.

parameters.name: ManagerApp
parameters.help: The PIM Manager app.

parameters.name: PrivateEndpointSubnetName
parameters.help: The private-endpoint subnet inside the PIM VNet (found or created).

parameters.name: PrivateEndpointSubnetAddressPrefix
parameters.help: A free range for that subnet inside the PIM VNet, e.g. 10.50.1.0/26. Required.

parameters.name: AcrAgentPoolName
parameters.help: The registry build pool (private builds; the updater job gets PIM_ACR_AGENT_POOL).

parameters.name: HubVnetId
parameters.help: The hub VNet resource id. Route Redeploy peers to it and links the private DNS zone; route Rebuild links the zone to each one given. Without it only the PIM VNet resolves the PIM Manager.

parameters.name: SkipPeering
parameters.help: The hub owner creates the hub side of the peering. The run STOPS at step 1 (exit 10) and prints the New-PimHubPrepareScript.ps1 command that writes the hub owner's script.

parameters.name: DeployPrincipalObjectId
parameters.help: Passed to New-PimHubPrepareScript.ps1: the object id of whoever runs the conversion, so the hub owner's script grants it its rights on the hub.

parameters.name: PrivateDnsResourceGroup
parameters.help: Where the private DNS zones go (same subscription).

parameters.name: SkipPrivateDns
parameters.help: Route Redeploy: do not create the private DNS zone for the new address (your own DNS answers for it).

parameters.name: EasyAuthAllowedPrincipals
parameters.help: Who may sign in to the PIM Manager (groups / users). Default: the existing assignments are kept.

parameters.name: EasyAuthAllowAllTenantUsers
parameters.help: Every member account in the tenant may sign in (never guests).

parameters.name: HostName
parameters.help: Optional stable custom name for the PIM Manager (step 6), e.g. pim.contoso.local. Needs your certificate.

parameters.name: KeyVaultName
parameters.help: With -HostName: the Key Vault holding the certificate.

parameters.name: KeyVaultCertName
parameters.help: With -HostName: the certificate's name in that Key Vault.

parameters.name: PfxPath
parameters.help: With -HostName: a PFX file instead of Key Vault.

parameters.name: PfxPassword
parameters.help: The PFX password (secure string; never saved in the state, pass it again on -Resume).

parameters.name: HostDns
parameters.help: With -HostName: Auto, PrivateDnsZone, AdDns (prints the record for you to add) or None.

parameters.name: HostDnsResourceGroup
parameters.help: With -HostName: the resource group of your existing private DNS zone for that name.

parameters.name: SqlPrivate
parameters.help: Step 7, last: add the SQL private endpoint, then save the private values in the deploy profile. Turning the SQL server's public access off stays your action.

parameters.name: HubSideDone
parameters.help: On -Resume after stop point 1: the hub owner has run the script.

parameters.name: ConfirmedFromInside
parameters.help: On -Resume after stop point 2: the private PIM Manager was verified from inside the network (Confirm-PimInstall.ps1 run there).

parameters.name: Reporter
parameters.help: Optional scriptblock called with one event per step: { step = { id; title }; state = started|ok|failed|waiting|skipped; message }.

parameters.name: InvardiaInstallToken
parameters.help: Optional: posts each step to Invardia's tracked installation (best effort; never fails the run).

parameters.name: Resume
parameters.help: Continue the recorded conversion after its last completed step (the first run's parameters fill everything not given again).

parameters.name: Apply
parameters.help: Run the steps. Without it (and always with -WhatIf) the script prints the full plan with each child command, signs in to nothing and changes nothing.

readsOnly: the deploy profile and the conversion state on this machine
the Container Apps environment and the PIM Manager (exposure, static IP, address)
the SQL database's point-in-time restore window
whether this machine reaches the PIM Manager's private address (name resolution and TCP 443 only)
network: graph.microsoft.com (the steps that grant the new identities)
<server>.database.windows.net:1433 (the steps that write database users and the profile deploy)
the PIM Manager's private address on TCP 443 (the inside check)
whatIf: Prints the resolved parameters (from the deploy profile and the command line), anything missing, and every step in the guide's order with the exact child command it would run (New-PimHubPrepareScript.ps1 for the hub owner, the capture, New-PimHostingPrerequisites.ps1, Remove-PimContainerStack.ps1, Invoke-PimDeployAll.ps1, Confirm-PimInstall.ps1, Set-PimManagerCustomHost.ps1), the two stop points, and 'PLAN ONLY -- nothing was signed in to and nothing was changed'. -WhatIf wins over -Apply.
undo: Before -Apply nothing changes. After a stop or a failure: -Resume -Apply continues, or the printed rollback applies (route Redeploy: Invoke-PimDeployAll.ps1 with the original profile brings the public environment back; route Rebuild: Rebuild-PimEnvExternal.ps1 -Apply). The data is never touched; the point-in-time restore point is recorded in the state file.
